study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose and evaluate a whole-brain normative modeling approach (FUNCOIN) for resting-state fMRI functional connectivity to detect individual-level abnormalities in complex brain disorders, and assess its clinical relevance in bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study explicitly uses UK Biobank rsfMRI data with over 60,000 subjects. Healthy subjects are divided into training (N=32,000) and testing (N=14,000) sets, with clinical groups for BD and PD also identified.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We use rsfMRI data from UKB (N >60,000 people) ... We divide the subjects into three groups: A large group of healthy subjects to train the model on (training data, N =32,000), a set of healthy subjects on which we test the out-of-sample performance of the model (test data, N =14,000), and a group of subjects with psychiatric or neurological diagnoses. We focused on chronic brain diseases that have been addressed in the rsfMRI FC literature and that have more than 100 subjects in the dataset: BD (N =101) and PD (N =132).

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper clearly states approximately 50,000 healthy subjects without psychiatric or neurological diagnoses, with 32,000 used for training and 14,000 for testing, totaling 46,000 analyzed healthy subjects.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: In this setting, we consider a subject healthy if they have no psychiatric or neurological diagnoses (group F or G diagnoses in ICD-10), which is the case for approximately 50000 of the subjects. We divide the subjects into three groups: A large group of healthy subjects to train the model on (training data, N =32,000), a set of healthy subjects on which we test the out-of-sample performance of the model (test data, N =14,000)...

rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: The age variable was linearly transformed the interval [0,1], with 0 and 1 corresponding to the minimum and maximum age in the whole dataset (44.56 and 85.43 years).

nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: Using data from UK Biobank (UKB) ... we create an integrative normative model of FC from 32000 individuals and test it on 14000 healthy subjects.

caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: ... one psychiatric and one neurological brain disease: bipolar disorder (BD) and Parkinson's disease (PD).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: BD and PD subjects show significantly higher likelihood of abnormal whole-brain FC patterns than controls; PD abnormalities are detectable up to 8 years before diagnosis; localized edgewise models did not show these effects.
